problem: A new immutable mesh previously allocated its own vertex buffer even when only its materials or index order differed from an existing mesh.
change: Exact complete vertex bytes identify one immutable GPU allocation and one owned CPU copy. Materials, index order, bounds and per-mesh draw commands stay independent. Dynamic meshes always retain their own writable storage.
ownership: A stable Host-owned map key retains bytes until the last mesh lease. No Native scene or atlas pointers survive callbacks. SDL continues to retain queued GPU uses after the final application release.
budget: Charge shared GPU bytes once; recalculate both vertex and index requirements if reserve evicts their last old lease. CPU memory counts the unique owned vertex key once. No new budget or quality reduction.
observation: Private benchmark arrays record actual static vertex allocations, reuses and pool bytes, including initialization. Existing complete frame clocks and numerical gates are unchanged.
limitations: Focused tests are not a Native game timing or a manual playthrough.
Full Windows1040/1807 CI, fresh balanced ordinary comparison and final unchanged binary qualification remain required.
This branch does not import the separate static SDL observer or its QPC wrappers.
